video_title: Lakers Sold Again In STUNNING $12.5 Billion Dollar Deal, What Does This Mean For LA?

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers have been sold for $12.5 billion in a stunning deal.
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers being refolded after a little more than a year to a group, I assume will be a group.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The Lakers being refolded after a little more than a year to a group, I assume will be a group because they'll continue to be selling pieces of this is my guess. But to a group with our old boss, Bob Iger.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: Howdy partners, I'd say you're always on BST, Wendy.

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: That was on the T for you, sir.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter's $2.5 billion profit on the Lakers sale in 10 months.
quotes.excerpt: He just made 2.5 billion in 10 months selling the Lakers.
quotes.quote: I had to take a minute too, Brian, when I first started getting wind of it, very late last night in Los Angeles. I couldn't even really wrap my head around this. Is this right? But you got to run those things down. We all get tips like that and you run them down. I went to bed thinking I was probably right, but I wasn't sure yet and then I woke up very early and I knew I was right. He just made 2.5 billion in 10 months selling the Lakers. I don't think that was the initial intention of buying the shares of the Lakers. There were grand plans with the Walter Group and the Dodgers and the Lakers. The way this came together is that Josh Kushner and Bob Iger were one of the big groups in Las Vegas and they've been trying to get an expansion team in Vegas. The bidding on that franchise has gotten close to that $10 billion number. That's the same price Mark Walter paid Jeanie Buss when he bought her shares of the Lakers.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter's Department of Justice investigation and the Lakers sale.
quotes.excerpt: There's been some reports over the last few months that Mark's under investigation with the Department of Justice.
quotes.quote: There's been some reports over the last few months that Mark's under investigation with the Department of Justice. Everyone involved says blank denial that this had anything to do with it, but you and I are smart, and Tim, you're also here. I mean, I couldn't resist. He just made 2.5 billion in 10 months selling the Lakers. I understand the business aspect. I think there were advantages to being liquid here to get all this money back into the accounts. I don't know, I'm speculating on that, but it's interesting and that's what everyone in the NBA is wondering and talking about because I certainly think when Mark bought the Lakers from Jeanie Buss, their intention was to own them for a very long time.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter's SEC investigation and potential financial motives for the Lakers sale.
quotes.excerpt: We know that Mark Walter is under investigation by the SEC.
quotes.quote: We know that Mark Walter is under investigation by the SEC. We are not insurance law specialists. We are not assistant US District Attorneys. We are not investigators. But he is under investigation. We know this because there is a suspicion that he might have put too much of his insurance company's money into his other businesses, which are referred to as affiliated companies. There's regulation on insurance companies and there's suspicion that maybe not all of the rules were followed. He was a stepped process where he and his partners bought 27% of the Lakers in 2021 and they gave Jeanie Buss a five-year transition window to remain as the governor, where after that they would do that. You don't do that if you're planning on flipping it. There are potentially reasons why he would want to get liquidity for his businesses. There's also reasons why he would want to potentially be able to show the SEC that he made an investment that returned a big profit for his insurance business.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Kushner's ownership stakes in the Miami Heat and Memphis Grizzlies.
quotes.excerpt: Josh Kushner is a minority owner of the Miami Heat and previously was a minority owner of the Memphis Grizzlies.
quotes.quote: Josh Kushner is a minority owner of the Miami Heat and previously was a minority owner of the Memphis Grizzlies and therefore has been approved to have that by the NBA. He has been vetted on some level by the NBA and approved by the NBA to own pieces of two different teams. In fact, he will have to sell his share of the Miami Heat, which by the way, the Heat don't sell shares very often. That's a very closely held team. He will have to sell the shares of the Miami Heat before he can buy the Lakers. That potentially could take some time as a side note.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Bob Iger's long-standing relationship with the NBA and its owners.
quotes.excerpt: Bob Iger has been a long-time close business associate with the NBA and its owners and top officials.
quotes.quote: Bob Iger has been a long-time close business associate with the NBA and its owners and top officials. As the CEO of Disney, he was part of the negotiations that have renewed multiple times to be the rights holder. This is our company at ESPN. We carry the NBA. Bob Iger has sat at negotiating tables with Adam Silver for years. There's obviously a relationship there. Also, Kushner and Iger and their group were raising money to make this Vegas team. They've been putting it together for months if not years to prepare to bid for Las Vegas. And so there was this ready-made and by the way, this is something that Mark Walter, if Mark Walter came to the point where he understood he had to sell the Lakers, it's not a bad time to sell a high asset when you've got all these potential ownership groups who have been working for a long time to put money together.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Bob Iger's statement to the California Post regarding the Lakers sale.
quotes.excerpt: It was suggested to us that maybe Mark Walter would be interested in selling his stake in the Lakers.
quotes.quote: Bob Iger gave an interview to Kobe Price, a Lakers beat writer for the California Post. He said, "We were involved in pursuing the new franchise in Vegas, and while that happened, it was suggested to us that maybe Mark Walter would be interested in selling his stake in the Lakers." A lot is in that sentence. I don't want to assume that that is the ironclad sentence, but it makes it sound like somebody came to them. I can speculate who that somebody was, but I'm not going to.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' current business operations following the ownership change.
quotes.excerpt: For now, this is business as usual with the Lakers.
quotes.quote: For now, this is business as usual with the Lakers. They've hired all these new people. They just completely redid the team. Luka Doncic is looking up going, "Wow, I thought it was strange in Dallas."

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Bloomberg report on Mark Walter's efforts to unwind his investments.
quotes.excerpt: Bloomberg reported in the last couple of weeks that Mark Walter has been looking to take businesses.
quotes.quote: Bloomberg reported in the last couple of weeks that Mark Walter has been looking to take businesses that he moved his insurance money into and unwind them so that he can get the money that he gave from his insurance company out of them. I do not want to make an assumption as to why he's doing that, but he's been reportedly investigated for maybe not 100% following all the laws putting his money into affiliated companies and now he's trying to take money out of the affiliated companies and put them back to insurance.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Schwartz's statement on the Lakers sale and CBA rules.
quotes.excerpt: Incredible, the Lakers sell for $12B, yet teams won't spend on older vets because of current CBA rules.
quotes.quote: A tweet comes out from Excel Basketball. From our founder and CEO, Jeff Schwartz: "Incredible, the Lakers sell for $12B, yet teams won't spend on older vets because of current CBA rules. Thank you, Union."

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's public profile management since joining the Lakers.
quotes.excerpt: Luka's management of his public profile since he's become a Laker has been excellent, largely.
quotes.quote: Luka's management of his public profile since he's become a Laker has been excellent, largely. Luka's ultimately all that matters is what he does on the court. But Luka's management of his public profile since he's become a Laker has been excellent, largely. He's been anyway, I don't want to get into that, but you know, inviting his team to Slovenia, the moves he's made, investing in the community in Los Angeles. I just think Luka's team Luka is operating well. Ultimately, player Luka has to win.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's statement on his commitment to the Lakers.
quotes.excerpt: Being a Laker means everything to me, and I'm excited to get back on the court.
quotes.quote: Being a Laker means everything to me, and I'm excited to get back on the court and bring a championship to LA. I've gotten used to big changes over these last few years, but I know that no matter what, there is no limit to the potential of this iconic franchise. I look forward to meeting Josh and Bob so we can get to work building something special in LA together.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's public statement on the Lakers' ownership changes.
quotes.excerpt: I've gotten used to big changes over these last few years.
quotes.quote: I've gotten used to big changes over these last few years. Okay, this is him saying. Okay, how many times we're going to sell? Is LeBron going to be on the team? No? Okay, fine. You know, so but this is him acknowledging.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter's history of ownership groups in the NBA.
quotes.excerpt: This is his fifth ownership group in a pretty quick span.
quotes.quote: He got backstabbed, traded in the middle of the night. Jeanie Buss sold or the Buss family sold. Now Mark Walter. I mean, it's just like this is his fifth ownership group in a pretty quick span.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: The timeline of the Mark Walter investigation and Lakers sale.
quotes.excerpt: The first investigation seems to have started in September of last year.
quotes.quote: The first investigation seems to have started in September of last year. The sale to Mark Walter is approved in October. So, did the NBA, were they fully apprised of what was going on behind the scenes when they approved this sale? I don't know that answer. That's something we all have to go look into and find out. But from what I understand, it was a fairly quick closing. He just wired $6 billion. Like he just had it and he wired it.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: The involvement of various ownership groups in the Lakers sale.
quotes.excerpt: The Buss family owns 17 or 18 percent.
quotes.quote: The Buss family owns 17 or 18 percent. And Patrick Soon-Shiong owns about 7%. I believe they're buying all of Mark's shares.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' business operations and the impact of new hires.
quotes.excerpt: They've hired all these new people. They've hired analytics guys, they've hired scouts, they've hired marketing people.
quotes.quote: They've hired all these new people. They've hired analytics guys, they've hired scouts, they've hired marketing people, they've hired business executives. They've hired the whole business operations. Andrew Friedman was advising Rob Pelinka. Farhan Zaidi, who was the GM of the Dodgers once, then he was the Giants GM, now he's back. He's the special advisor for Mark Walter. He's been very involved with Rob Pelinka and the whole front office there and the hiring. All of these things have been set in motion.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' roster construction and long-term contracts.
quotes.excerpt: They signed guys to four-year deals. This team they put together on Luka, this is a team.
quotes.quote: They signed guys to four-year deals. This team they put together on Luka, this is a team that is built to stay together, right? They don't have a lot of flexibility now after giving up the two draft picks for Walker Kessler. Quentin Grimes got a four-year deal. Sandro Mamukelashvili got a four-year deal. It's really, I'm getting good at it now. I really worked on that one. We have to say it all the time, so I got to, I just have to get that nailed, right? Four-year deal for some role players, and that's a lot. And the idea is they wanted that group to grow together.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter's investment strategy and the Lakers' valuation.
quotes.excerpt: Mark bought 26% at a $5 billion valuation, then he bought the rest of it at a $10 billion.
quotes.quote: Mark bought 26% at a $5 billion valuation, then he bought the rest of it at a $10 billion valuation. So he's actually done better. It's like, just think of it like a stock, okay? If you bought the stock at five and then it goes up to 10, the first shares you bought really are worth a lot more now, okay? And then the ones at 10 are worth a lot. Okay, so that's right.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' valuation and the potential for a quick sale.
quotes.excerpt: I would be stunned if this was ever viewed as a flip.
quotes.quote: I would be stunned if this was ever viewed as a flip. I don't know. I would be stunned if this was ever viewed as a flip. I don't think it was ever viewed as a flip. I would say, I don't think it's incorrect to to conclude that two very smart businessmen saw another businessman who's dealing with some legal issues and took the opportunity to pounce.
